scope: Proposition F.2 (Constrained sampling) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 137-138. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Prescribe a finite collection of input caps, testing complexities, slice bounds, and requested accuracies at the pre stage. Assume the system has rank at least R in Definition F.1, with R and the side lengths chosen sufficiently large in the order (F.2). For every tuple of centers, the construction gives one ensemble satisfying all the prescribed requirements, with bounds uniform in the centers, the inputs, and the path-dependent slice and test choices within those requirements. All later choices are made for this prescribed collection; changing the requested accuracies permits a new construction. The ensemble consists of integer affine maps ψ(t) = x + V t from a box T = Qm j=1{0, . . . , Tj − 1}, where m was fixed as a polynomial of 1 + n + P h dh before all testing and accuracy budgets, Tj ≤ L, and some sides have length L. The ensemble has the following properties. 1. Each ψ(T ) lies in U, and the functions yh ◦ ψ are fully slow polynomial lifts while βh ◦ ψ have integer ordinary coefficients, all of degrees at most h. Noninjective maps have negligible probability. If the centers are mixed independently with Haar measure, the one-site law, with t uniform, approximates the uniform law on U at the prescribed forward accuracy against every unit-bounded input. 2. A permitted site twist is a bounded Lipschitz function of u/H, (yh)h, multiplied by buffered chart cutoffs and by characters or residue indicators of (u, βh)h of a pre-bounded common modulus. For fixed centers, suppose a pre-large fraction of sampled maps detects an arbitrary pre-bounded function ϕ : U → C, on a pre-cost slice of T , against a bounded local niltest of degree r, with 0 ≤ r ≤ s, and pre complexity. The slices and niltests may be chosen separately 137 for each map. Then ϕ has a pre-large correlation on U with a permitted twist times a bounded ambient degree-r niltest of pre complexity. More precisely, write X(ϕ) = Eψ sup B,F |Et∈Bϕ(ψ(t))F(t)| , where B, F range over the prescribed slices and tests. Every fixed unit-bounded input admits an approximation in X, to any prescribed pre accuracy, by a linear combination of the indicated ambient twisted niltests. The number of terms and the sum of the absolute coefficients have pre bounds. 3. Let T∗(u, β) be a fixed positive patch formula with d∗ further slots, in which u has weight 1 and βh has weight h, and with pre-bounded complexity. If 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1, and a pre-large fraction of maps have a pre-cost slice on which Et(f(ψ(t)) − λ)T∗(ψ(t), β(ψ(t))) ≥ e−bpre , then, for fixed ε > 0, a slice of U supports a positive patch of rank at most d∗ + P h dim Wh and an inverse-exponential-in-polynomial score against f − (1 − ε)λ. The output complexity, slice cost, and logarithmic inverse score in this item alone may charge the logarithmic heights of bases of Wh and log R, log L. There is also an unconstrained version of items 1 and 2: for every fixed ℓ ≥ ℓ0(s) one may prescribe the ℓ integer side lengths in advance, provided they are sufficiently large and pairwise comparable. In particular they may be prescribed distinct comparable primes. Its integer spatial law is dominated by a uniform product-box law at scales Hi and Hi/L by a pre-bounded factor, as required for Proposition E.1. The choice of ℓ is fixed before all testing and accuracy budgets; all constants may depend on it.
